newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: SOCCER-COSTA RICA ANGRY OVER CANADIAN OFFICIAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-COSTA RICA ANGRY OVER CANADIAN OFFICIAL.

text.p: Costa Rica's coach criticised world soccer authority FIFA on Sunday for naming an official from Canada, one of their direct rivals for a World Cup place, as an observer for next Sunday's qualifier at home to Mexico.

"Costa Rica is a dangerous rival for certain interests," said Horacio Cordero. "It is extraordinary that they name as observer an official for one of the countries that is taking part in the qualifying matches."

Costa Rica, Canada and Mexico are in a six-team group which will decide the three CONCACAF representatives in next year's World Cup in France. The other teams are the United States, El Salvador and Jamaica.
Cordero, an Argentine, made a desperate plea to fans for good behaviour. "We have to be extremely careful," he said.
Carlos Zuniga, vice-president of the Costa Rican soccer federation, said the Canadian official would arrive on Monday and stay until the match was over.
Costa Rica were fined the equivalent of $7,000 by FIFA for crowd incidents following their 2-1 home win over the United States in an earlier stage of the qualifying competition, local officials said.
The ban was imposed after reports that fans had thrown objects on to the pitch and at the team bus and that their players had been spat upon.
Zuniga said security would be reinforced for next Sunday's match. He said the biggest worry was that further incidents could result in the team being forced to play home matches outside the country.
